title: An unchanged straight bend test can conceal different curved response
statement: Four finite inextensible/unshearable static shooting settings use quaternion RK4/Newton and terminal moment zero; they are not stability, uniqueness or continuum-error proofs. At C=40 N m^2, results are straight 7.63134584 mm/1.277332 degrees, ordered program 7.56664355/1.274648, and uniform (0,-2) 8.00168629/1.379758. Changing only C to 4 leaves the straight test unchanged but gives curved linear 23.4343386 mm/6.929326 degrees and nonlinear 23.2868569/6.891268. Small residuals and refinement agreement are finite checks. Nonlinear calculations omit the shear/stretch included in the linear ones, so their difference is not a pure nonlinear correction. C=.4 large first-variation rotations are outside the screen, not actual finite-deformation measurements.
